teaser.text: Ares Management Corporation is a hired investment manager: it puts other people’s money to work and charges for the judgment and machinery that make that possible. To follow a dollar through the business, separate the capital owned by its funds and clients from the fees Ares earns for managing it.

stock.opening: Ares’ weighted price is $123.76 in October 2029, with bear and base probabilities of 29% and 52%, and bull at 19%. Ares’ outlook hinges on converting fee-paying assets into earnings while credit stress and dilution remain contained.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains Ares’ business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Ares’ shares be in the forecast years?

paragraphs.text: The probability-weighted outcome is modest initially but improves over three years. The weighted price is $109.04 in October 2027, excluding dividends. That is a 1% return from today's $113.07. It reaches $114.89 in October 2028, a 12% return, and $123.76 in October 2029, a 26% return.
The October 2029 range is wide, from $58.44 in the bear case to $225.87 in the bull case. The bear probability is 29%, while the base case receives 52%. The bull probability is 19%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Ares, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The base is anchored by the $5.76937 next-twelve-month EPS estimate, which implies about $1,306 million of earnings at roughly 226.3 million public shares. First-half FRE was up 20%, but ARCC non-accruals rose from 1.8% to 2.4%, so growth is credible without being certain. Management's 16%–20% FRE target supports the base and bull paths, but is not a net-income guarantee.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Ares really make?

paragraphs.text: Stock pay adds a second distinction. Subtracting it from free cash flow produces this memo’s “real free cash flow,” which recognizes dilution as an ownership cost. It does not mean that the stock awards were cash paid that year. Working capital also matters because receivables and compensation payable can shift cash between periods.

dividend.title: Ares dividend: history, cash cover and yield
dividend.meta_description: Ares dividend history, cash coverage, future plans and current yield, explained in plain English.
dividend.opening: Ares raised its regular quarterly dividend to $1.35 per share in February 2026, after dividends paid rose from $309,835 thousand to $985,543 thousand across the five-year period. Cash coverage is not straightforward: the common dividend exceeded GAAP EPS in 2025, while consolidated fund activity can obscure cash available to Ares shareholders and June 2026 free cash flow was negative after capital spending.
dividend.closing: The full memo also explains Ares’s business, rivals, management plans and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Ares pay its shareholders?

paragraphs.text: Ares also increased shareholder distributions. Dividends paid rose from $309,835 thousand to $985,543 thousand across the five-year period, while no shares were repurchased. In February 2026, Ares raised its regular quarterly dividend to $1.35 per share and renewed $750.0 million of repurchase authority, but made no program repurchases during the first half. Authority is permission to spend, not money already returned. The cash therefore supported both growth and a larger commitment to shareholders, bringing the question back to whether acquisitions created enough earnings to justify their cost.

blocks.heading: Is Ares’s dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: The June 2026 fee deferral shows the same problem in miniature. Ares could recognize incentive fees from Ares Capital Corporation while collection waited for a contractual hurdle. The common dividend exceeded GAAP EPS in 2025, but coverage requires recurring fee earnings, realized income, ownership claims and actual distributions to be reconciled.

Cash supplied the sharper warning. June operating cash flow was negative even though net income was positive, and free cash flow was negative after capital spending. Across the half-year, company entities generated about $1.021 billion of operating cash, while consolidated funds used $766.1 million and eliminations reduced the total further.

blocks.heading: What is Ares’s dividend yield today?

paragraphs.text: Ares traded at $113.07 on October 19, 2026. Its next-twelve-month P/E was 19.6x against a trailing P/E of 51.9x. The dividend yield was 4.8%. Revenue grew 44.2% in 2025, but diluted EPS fell to $1.71 from $2.04 in 2024. Ares’ own real free cash flow turned positive in the latest two years after three negative years; per share it was $11.29 in 2025 versus $11.85 in 2024. Reported net debt includes consolidated funds, not only corporate borrowing.

blocks.heading: What has Ares guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: That timing hurt Ares early in 2026. Management cut its preliminary first-quarter realized net performance-income estimate from approximately $100 million to approximately $75 million, mainly because European-style funds had not yet reached the necessary distribution point. It still expected more than $350 million for full-year 2026. On September 30, it estimated approximately $10 million for the third quarter, which covered one earnings component rather than the whole year.

The longer-term ambition is also clear. From 2023 through 2028, Ares targets annual compound growth of 16%–20% in fee-related earnings and 20%–25% in realized income. For 2026, it expected fee-related earnings margin improvement near the upper end of its zero-to-150-basis-point range. The upper end means roughly 1.5 percentage points more fee profit per dollar of relevant revenue.

blocks.heading: Has Ares kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Ares exceeded its promise to reach at least $500 billion of AUM by the end of 2025. Management has emphasized reinvesting for continued growth rather than maximizing immediate margins. That record supports its credibility as a builder, but the final test is durable earnings per share after compensation, dilution, and other claims.

blocks.heading: How have Ares revenue and profit trended?

paragraphs.text: Revenue, operating income, net income and diluted EPS all increased from the year-earlier quarter. FRE reached about $491.1 million, up 20%. The every-other-year investor meeting added about $9 million to second-quarter general and administrative expense, so calendar effects influenced the comparison.

blocks.heading: What should readers watch in Ares's next results?

paragraphs.text: Ares’s third-quarter results call is scheduled for October 29, 2026. The important question is how management connects the preliminary performance-income estimate with its full-year expectation. Specific expected realizations would provide more visibility than a general claim that portfolios are performing well, because a sale slipping past December 31 can move income into another year.
